## 03:10Z — STARK v1: demo-only q warning (sheriff SHF-20261106-a114e7, V1) (Claude, session 01TCbLH7MMjkGjb1os2EZfoL)

- Owner ruling on V1, relayed by the commissioning session: keep the caller-chosen `q`, add a warning.
- `src/zk/stark.rs`:
  - The module docs, `prove`, `verify` and `statement_transcript` now say that the v1 path is demo-only and unsound by design at small `q`, and point to `stark_v2`.
  - New `V1_SAFE_BITS = 64`, `v1_safe_query_count(n) = spot_check_queries(n, 64)` and `v1_query_count_warning(n, q)`. `prove` and `verify` print the warning to stderr when `q` is below the threshold.
  - Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: no new errors, and no floor on `q`.
- New test `v1_warns_below_the_sized_query_count_only`: the warning fires below the threshold and not at or above it, for n in {2, 8, 64, 1024}. Sizes the entry points reject get no warning. q = 20 at n = 8 (the grinding demo) warns, and the n = 8 threshold is 333.

- Threshold: the module's own spot-check analysis. `spot_check_queries(n, bits)` is the least q with (1 − 1/n)^q ≤ 2^−bits, and `grinding_fails_at_sized_query_count` already uses 64 bits as "the verifier's sized q". No new number was invented. The docs call it a demo threshold, not an audited security level.
- The warning goes to stderr on every call below the threshold ("loud"). The test harness captures it, so the 20,000-attempt grinding demo test produces no visible noise unless run with `--nocapture`.
- The warning text is a pure function, `v1_query_count_warning`, so a test can assert exactly when it fires.

- None beyond the PR.

- A first draft asserted the n = 8 threshold as 155; the module's own test comment, (6/8)^333, shows it is 333. Corrected before running.

## 2026-11-07T19:45Z — koblitz_symmetrised `sat_loop`: block models at level 0 (Claude)


- Picked up the open thread from 2026-10-27 (`koblitz_symmetrised.rs:1033`).
  Branch `claude/koblitz-symmetrised-resolve-reset` from origin/main a2be660914.
- Added `sat_loop_blocks_models_with_root_fixed_variables`: x0 = x1 = 1,
  x2..x4 free (8 models), `max_models = 100`. On unfixed main it fails with
  `model 31 returned twice` (verified, `cargo test --release --lib
  koblitz_symmetrised::tests::sat_loop_blocks`).
- Fix in `src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_symmetrised.rs` `sat_loop`: call
  `enc.solver.reset_search()` before adding the blocking clause.
  `cargo test --release --lib koblitz_symmetrised`: 18 passed, 0 failed.


- Fixed the caller, not `Solver::add_clause`: `model()` reads the live
  trail, so a backjump inside `add_clause` would silently erase models for
  any of the ~154 callers that add a clause and then read the model.
- Mechanism: `add_clause` drops root-false literals only at level 0; above
  it a blocking clause can be watched on two root-false literals, which are
  never unassigned, so the clause is never visited. Effect in `sat_loop`:
  repeated models until `max_models`, then `complete = false` instead of a
  proved UNSAT (lost completeness and wasted effort, not a wrong relation:
  every returned relation is still lifted and checked).


- Other callers that add clauses after SAT without `reset_search()` were not
  re-audited in this entry (the 2026-10-27 audit covered re-solve after
  `Unknown`, not after SAT).


- Conductor CLI not installed in this container; no reservation claimed.

## 2026-11-07T19:45Z — koblitz_symmetrised `sat_loop`: block models at level 0 (Claude)


- Picked up the open thread from 2026-10-27 (`koblitz_symmetrised.rs:1033`).
  Branch `claude/koblitz-symmetrised-resolve-reset` from origin/main a2be660914.
- Added `sat_loop_blocks_models_with_root_fixed_variables`: x0 = x1 = 1,
  x2..x4 free (8 models), `max_models = 100`. On unfixed main it fails with
  `model 31 returned twice` (verified, `cargo test --release --lib
  koblitz_symmetrised::tests::sat_loop_blocks`).
- Fix in `src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_symmetrised.rs` `sat_loop`: call
  `enc.solver.reset_search()` before adding the blocking clause.
  `cargo test --release --lib koblitz_symmetrised`: 18 passed, 0 failed.


- Fixed the caller, not `Solver::add_clause`: `model()` reads the live
  trail, so a backjump inside `add_clause` would silently erase models for
  any of the ~154 callers that add a clause and then read the model.
- Mechanism: `add_clause` drops root-false literals only at level 0; above
  it a blocking clause can be watched on two root-false literals, which are
  never unassigned, so the clause is never visited. Effect in `sat_loop`:
  repeated models until `max_models`, then `complete = false` instead of a
  proved UNSAT (lost completeness and wasted effort, not a wrong relation:
  every returned relation is still lifted and checked).


- Other callers that add clauses after SAT without `reset_search()` were not
  re-audited in this entry (the 2026-10-27 audit covered re-solve after
  `Unknown`, not after SAT).


- Conductor CLI not installed in this container; no reservation claimed.

  - New `V1_SAFE_BITS = 64`, `v1_safe_query_count(n) = spot_check_queries(n, 64)` and `v1_query_count_warning(n, q)`. `prove` and `verify` print the warning to stderr when `q` is below the threshold.
  - Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: no new errors, and no floor on `q`.
- New test `v1_warns_below_the_sized_query_count_only`: the warning fires below the threshold and not at or above it, for n in {2, 8, 64, 1024}. Sizes the entry points reject get no warning. q = 20 at n = 8 (the grinding demo) warns, and the n = 8 threshold is 333.

- Threshold: the module's own spot-check analysis. `spot_check_queries(n, bits)` is the least q with (1 − 1/n)^q ≤ 2^−bits, and `grinding_fails_at_sized_query_count` already uses 64 bits as "the verifier's sized q". No new number was invented. The docs call it a demo threshold, not an audited security level.
- The warning goes to stderr on every call below the threshold ("loud"). The test harness captures it, so the 20,000-attempt grinding demo test produces no visible noise unless run with `--nocapture`.
- The warning text is a pure function, `v1_query_count_warning`, so a test can assert exactly when it fires.

- None beyond the PR.

- A first draft asserted the n = 8 threshold as 155; the module's own test comment, (6/8)^333, shows it is 333. Corrected before running.

## 19:55Z — Subgroup traps in lift-dense factor bases (Claude)

- Investigated why the C1 control A0 (y² + xy = x³ + 1) found 0 decompositions at k = 7 and 9 (#2704 H-Y1/H-Y3).
- Froze `research/subgroup_trap_20261107/PROTOCOL.md` at `7ac2099b8`. Amendment 1 (the trap condition is [K:F_2] < N and 2[K:F_2] ≠ N) was committed at `fe8b2b62e`; both were before any computation.
- Instrument: std-only Rust that reuses the frozen C1 sources by `#[path]` (FREEZE.sha256 OK), plus its own GF(2^N) code for the audit.
- Ran `run-20261107T2` (final; `run-20261107T1` agrees on every frozen field). Results [pcc:unverified], claim `PCC-20261107-286789`:
  - P1 PASS: A0's factor bases lie in H = E(F_Q) + ker(σ_Q + 1). Nonzero counts appear only on H (9 of 20,000 targets at k = 5; 0 of 8,000 and 0 of 1,500 at k = 7 and 9).
  - P2 PASS: ΣN over E(F_{Q²}) = m⁴ exactly, and the support is exactly H (484 and 8,236 points at k = 5 and 7).
  - P3 PASS: 0 of 309,870 targets with Tr(x_R) ≠ Tr(a) have a nonzero count; the 2E half carries 2.007× the prediction (median).
  - P4 PASS: every applicable line in #2686/#2704 has [K:F_2] = N.
  - Identity: the regenerated targets reproduce all 72 frozen rows.
- Wrote README, REPORT.pdf and `fig_subgroup_trap.{svg,png}`. Opened PR #3646.

- The #2704 verdicts stay as registered. This study explains the failures and does not re-score them.
- Post hoc correction: the borderline case 2[K:F_2] = N is not benign. A0 `tw_b` leaves 72–74 % of its 2E targets at zero, against 25–31 % on a full-degree line. Construction rule: use a line only when [K:F_2] = N.
- The odd-n factor 2^{n+1} is reported as derived accounting, not an improvement; it is the known cofactor mechanism.

- Formalise T1 and T2 in Lean, if wanted. The `.lake` cache was deleted to free disk; rebuild it with `lake exe cache get`.
- The odd-n accounting (Oakley 64× against plain F_q) is untested.

- The disk filled during `git fetch` of 11 days of main. I cleared caches, target dirs and the 7.7 GB Lean `.lake`.
- `/usr/bin/time` is missing, so the first background run did nothing; I re-ran it with bash timing.
- The scorer crashed on a NaN ratio (0/0 on NEG's empty bases). The producer now writes null, and the final run was regenerated with the fix.
- I ran k = 5 before filling `.resume/RESUME.md`. That file is tracked and holds another session's in-flight state, and there is no AWS identity for the upload, so the pushed branch serves as the checkpoint.
- KB unavailable: no `research-kb` binary, and the MCP server was not connected. I used the lead atlas and `rg` instead (sources listed in the README).

## 2026-11-07T19:45Z — koblitz_symmetrised `sat_loop`: block models at level 0 (Claude)


- Picked up the open thread from 2026-10-27 (`koblitz_symmetrised.rs:1033`).
  Branch `claude/koblitz-symmetrised-resolve-reset` from origin/main a2be660914.
- Added `sat_loop_blocks_models_with_root_fixed_variables`: x0 = x1 = 1,
  x2..x4 free (8 models), `max_models = 100`. On unfixed main it fails with
  `model 31 returned twice` (verified, `cargo test --release --lib
  koblitz_symmetrised::tests::sat_loop_blocks`).
- Fix in `src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_symmetrised.rs` `sat_loop`: call
  `enc.solver.reset_search()` before adding the blocking clause.
  `cargo test --release --lib koblitz_symmetrised`: 18 passed, 0 failed.


- Fixed the caller, not `Solver::add_clause`: `model()` reads the live
  trail, so a backjump inside `add_clause` would silently erase models for
  any of the ~154 callers that add a clause and then read the model.
- Mechanism: `add_clause` drops root-false literals only at level 0; above
  it a blocking clause can be watched on two root-false literals, which are
  never unassigned, so the clause is never visited. Effect in `sat_loop`:
  repeated models until `max_models`, then `complete = false` instead of a
  proved UNSAT (lost completeness and wasted effort, not a wrong relation:
  every returned relation is still lifted and checked).


- Other callers that add clauses after SAT without `reset_search()` were not
  re-audited in this entry (the 2026-10-27 audit covered re-solve after
  `Unknown`, not after SAT).


- Conductor CLI not installed in this container; no reservation claimed.

- Owner ruling on V1, relayed by the commissioning session: keep the caller-chosen `q`, add a warning.
- `src/zk/stark.rs`:
  - The module docs, `prove`, `verify` and `statement_transcript` now say that the v1 path is demo-only and unsound by design at small `q`, and point to `stark_v2`.
  - New `V1_SAFE_BITS = 64`, `v1_safe_query_count(n) = spot_check_queries(n, 64)` and `v1_query_count_warning(n, q)`. `prove` and `verify` print the warning to stderr when `q` is below the threshold.
  - Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: no new errors, and no floor on `q`.
- New test `v1_warns_below_the_sized_query_count_only`: the warning fires below the threshold and not at or above it, for n in {2, 8, 64, 1024}. Sizes the entry points reject get no warning. q = 20 at n = 8 (the grinding demo) warns, and the n = 8 threshold is 333.

- Threshold: the module's own spot-check analysis. `spot_check_queries(n, bits)` is the least q with (1 − 1/n)^q ≤ 2^−bits, and `grinding_fails_at_sized_query_count` already uses 64 bits as "the verifier's sized q". No new number was invented. The docs call it a demo threshold, not an audited security level.
- The warning goes to stderr on every call below the threshold ("loud"). The test harness captures it, so the 20,000-attempt grinding demo test produces no visible noise unless run with `--nocapture`.
- The warning text is a pure function, `v1_query_count_warning`, so a test can assert exactly when it fires.

- None beyond the PR.

- A first draft asserted the n = 8 threshold as 155; the module's own test comment, (6/8)^333, shows it is 333. Corrected before running.
